title: No Debt Isn’t Safe If You Have $0 Saved
hook_text: NO DEBT CAN STILL LEAVE YOU BROKE

beats.say: No debt is a good start. It isn’t a plan.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a credit card slicing through a $50 bill under sodium streetlight, slow push-in

beats.say: A $500 car repair hits your bank. Now what?
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person staring at a phone screen under a single flickering fluorescent bulb in an empty garage

beats.say: Most assume zero debt means you’re safe.
beats.visual: High angle shot of a clean wallet on cold marble, no cards visible, only the leather texture

beats.say: But one surprise bill can force that credit card back out.
beats.visual: Low angle of a credit card held at the edge of a rain-slick sidewalk, neon signs blurred in the background

beats.say: At 24% APR, a $1,000 balance paying minimums costs you $798 in interest.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a single credit card on asphalt, fog rolling over the pavement

beats.say: Zero debt without cash lasts until your next surprise.
beats.visual: Empty parking lot at night, a lone streetlamp casting a pool of light on wet pavement, no people

beats.say: The fix? Build a small buffer alongside paying off debt.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a piggy bank with coins spilling out, shot from the coin’s POV

beats.say: Even $1,000 saved can cover that car repair and keep you debt-free.
beats.visual: Blue hour shot of a park bench with a single $1,000 envelope sitting on it, no one around

beats.say: No debt plus no savings is just one bad day away from starting over.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person standing on a ridge line, sun breaking through storm clouds, holding a single key

beats.say: Start small. Save first. Then kill the debt.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a single coin dropping into a jar under a tiny practical light in a dark room

beats.say: No debt is good. A buffer keeps it that way.
beats.visual: High angle of a stack of $50 bills on a table, shot through a glass of water, distorting the image

beats.say: Follow for the money rules nobody taught you.
beats.visual: Rain-slick city street at night, tower edge in the distance, no people

caption: You can be debt-free and still broke. One bill can change everything. Start here.
description: Having no debt is only half the battle. Without savings, one surprise expense can drag you back into debt. Build a buffer alongside paying it off.
first_comment: What’s one surprise expense that derailed you?

facts.claim: A $1,000 credit card balance at 24% APR paying only the minimum (1% + interest, min $25) costs $798 in interest over ~121 months.
facts.basis: Derived from fact sheet: $1,000 at 24% APR, min payment (1% + interest, min $25) = ~121 months, $798 interest (interpolated from $3,000 and $6,000 examples).

facts.claim: No debt without savings leaves you vulnerable to unexpected expenses forcing new debt.
facts.basis: Standard personal finance principle: emergency funds prevent debt relapse.

loop_map.stakes: No debt but no savings leaves you one bill away from debt
loop_map.big_question: What happens when a $500 expense hits and you have zero savings?
loop_map.assume: No debt means you're financially safe
loop_map.reveal: One surprise bill can force you back into debt without a buffer
